blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Strategic supply planning, at senior level, is about shaping supply capacity and inventory to match not merely next month's demand, but the company's strategic direction. A firm that wants to grow in a new region must decide, well in advance, where production capacity will come from. A firm that wants to protect its margins against a known raw material shock must lay in inventory before the price moves. And a firm expecting a regulatory change must switch suppliers months before the change lands.

Such decisions cannot be left to monthly operational planning. They demand their own rhythm — quarterly strategic reviews where capacity, inventory and sourcing are weighed together, and where the planning team recommends that the company take specific, visible positions.

The test of a strategic supply plan is whether it still makes sense in twelve months under multiple scenarios. If it only holds in the central case, it is an operational plan dressed up as strategic. The distinction matters when reality arrives and the central case turns out to be the least likely version of the future.

items.q: According to the text, strategic supply planning matches supply capacity to…
items.why: "…to match not merely next month's demand, but the company's strategic direction."

items.q: What rhythm does strategic supply planning require, according to the text?
items.why: "They demand their own rhythm — quarterly strategic reviews…"

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Monthly operational planning cannot carry strategic supply decisions.
Capacity, inventory and sourcing should be considered together.
Supply decisions must sometimes be made months ahead of an event.
A plan that only works in the central case is genuinely strategic.
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que um plano que só vale no cenário central é 'operacional disfarçado de estratégico' — logo o autor discordaria de chamá-lo de estratégico.

items.q: The final sentence about the central case suggests that…
options: a plan should be robust because the expected future often does not materialise
planners should ignore scenarios other than the central one
twelve months is too short a horizon for planning
the central case is always the most accurate forecast
items.why: Inferência: se o cenário central costuma ser 'a versão menos provável do futuro', o plano precisa aguentar vários cenários, não só o esperado.

items.q: Laying in inventory before a raw material price moves is an example of…
options: postponing a decision until reality arrives
taking a deliberate position ahead of a known shock
items.why: "…must lay in inventory before the price moves" — é uma posição tomada com antecedência frente a um choque conhecido.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie conduzindo a primeira revisão estratégica trimestral com a diretoria. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for making the time. Before we open the numbers, let me be clear about what this review is not. This is not the monthly demand call. We are not here to fine-tune next quarter's orders. We are here to decide where this business chooses to be exposed over the next three years.

So I have built the plan around three scenarios, not one. The central case, yes — but also a hard tightening in the origin markets, and a regulatory shift on two of our key inputs. Notice that the plan behaves very differently in each. Under the central case, sitting tight is perfectly comfortable. Under the other two, comfort in month one becomes a very expensive problem by month nine.

My recommendation is straightforward. I recommend that we approve dual sourcing on the four critical inputs now, and that the board authorise us to build inventory ahead of the price move rather than after it. I am not asking you to bet on my forecast. I am asking that we take positions that survive whichever of these three futures actually arrives. If we only plan for the one we like best, we are not planning at all.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Sophie describe the purpose of this review?
options: To cut the number of suppliers
To decide where the business chooses to be exposed over three years
To review last month's demand figures
items.why: "We are here to decide where this business chooses to be exposed over the next three years."

items.q: How many scenarios has Sophie built the plan around?
items.why: "I have built the plan around three scenarios, not one" — cenário central, aperto nos mercados de origem e mudança regulatória.

items.q: What two positions does Sophie recommend the board take?
options: Approve dual sourcing and build inventory ahead of the price move
Cut inventory and delay sourcing decisions
Consolidate to a single supplier for cost certainty
Wait for the price move and then react
items.why: "I recommend that we approve dual sourcing… and that the board authorise us to build inventory ahead of the price move."

items.q: When Sophie says "comfort in month one becomes a very expensive problem by month nine", she implies that…
options: an easy choice now can prove costly if a harsher scenario unfolds
the plan should be revisited every month
doing nothing is safe under every scenario
the central case is the most likely outcome
items.why: Inferência: 'sitting tight' é confortável só no cenário central; nos outros dois, a inação sai cara mais adiante.

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "If we only plan for the one we like best, we are not planning at all"?
options: The board should pick the cheapest option
Forecasts are always accurate if they are optimistic
Choosing a single favourable scenario is not genuine planning
Planning is unnecessary when the future is uncertain
items.why: Inferência: planejar só para o cenário preferido ignora os riscos — não é planejamento estratégico de verdade.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The plan must serve the firm's strategic direction, not just this quarter's orders." Strategic direction refers to…
options: the long-term course the company has chosen to pursue
the current stock level in the warehouse
the org chart of the planning team
items.why: Strategic direction = direção estratégica: o rumo de longo prazo que a empresa escolheu.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We must lay in inventory before the ___ moves, or the margin is gone."
items.why: O contexto é proteger a margem contra a alta de preço — 'before the price moves'.

items.q: "The forecast holds only in the central case." The central case is…
options: the office where planning is done
the outcome the planners expect as most likely
items.why: Central case = cenário central: o desfecho tido como mais provável, em torno do qual se planeja.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "To grow in the new region we need more production ___, so we are commissioning a second plant."
items.why: Capacity = capacidade produtiva; ampliar a operação exige mais capacidade.

items.q: "A pending regulatory change forced us to switch suppliers early." A regulatory change is…
options: an alteration in the rules or laws that govern the business
a revision of the internal budget
a change in the delivery schedule
items.why: Regulatory change = mudança regulatória: alteração nas normas ou leis que regem a operação.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem em revisões estratégicas de supply. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The board still has to sign off on the dual-sourcing plan." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will lay in inventory ahead of the price move." To lay in means to…
options: build up a stock in advance
items.why: Lay in = estocar / acumular com antecedência, antes de precisar.

items.q: "Two directors pushed back on the early switch of suppliers." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, contestar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "None of these tweaks will move the needle on our exposure." This means they will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, produzir uma diferença perceptível.

items.q: "We agreed the plan last quarter but never followed through on the sourcing switch." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado; aqui, o oposto — não foi concluído.
